text:
Maria: Quick check-in on rerank API decisions before I lock the roadmap item. Need final on top_k meaning (returned vs scored), server normalization behavior, truncation policy, and hosted GA caps. SearchX expects 1k support but we should be pragmatic. @Ajay @Liam @Zara any final calls?

Ajay: My preference: keep request ergonomics simple. Clients send candidates[] (id, text, optional pre_score, optional meta). Params: top_k, score_mode (none|minmax|softmax|zscore), max_score_candidates (internal cap), and page_token for pagination. top_k always means how many results we return.

Ajay: Example request shape:
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query":"cheap flights to tokyo",
  "candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"..."},{"id":"c2","text":"...","pre_score":0.3}],
  "top_k":30,
  "score_mode":"softmax"
}
```

Liam: Operational guardrails for GA hosted: reject or gate huge jobs. Proposal: ingest cap 2000 candidate items, but default scored cap = 200 for hosted; top_k <= 200. Payload byte cap = 4MB. If inbound > caps, return 413 (payload too large) with hints or 429 (quota) depending on tenant limits.

Zara: Normalization should be opt-in. Default score_mode="none". When we normalize we must include a score_origin tag per result: "client" (pre_score), "server" (reranker), or "mixed". Also add normalization_method in the response so users know what transform we applied.

Ajay: Implementation note: for mixed inputs (some client pre_scores, some not) we compute server scores for missing entries then normalize across the union. For zscore we detect tiny variance and fallback to minmax to avoid NaNs.

Maria: Tie-breaker stability important. Use deterministic sort for equal scores (candidate id lexicographic). Also expose sorted_by field in response.

Liam: SLA targets to put in docs: p95 <= 120ms for top_k<=25, p95 <= 250ms for top_k<=100, p95 <= 350ms for top_k<=200. Recommend Dedicated for consistently higher throughput/recall.

Ajay: Memory-friendly runtime: streaming scoring + fixed-size min-heap for top_k selection. Quick byte-length pre-check to avoid tokenizing everything; only tokenize when within limits. Consider an experimental approx=true path (ANN-ish) for very large candidate sets — opt-in only.

Zara: Truncation rules proposal: per-candidate default token limit = 512 (tenant-configurable), request-level quick byte cap = 4MB for hosted. If pre-check fails, respond 413 and include header X-Rerank-Detail: payload_too_large and X-Rerank-Suggest-Split: true.

Ajay: SDK helpers: provide a client-side pager that splits candidate arrays into multiple requests, then merges and re-ranks results client-side (we'll publish example code). That lets customers approximate large recall without hosted changes.

Liam: Metrics: emit requests_total, candidates_scored_total, avg_candidate_bytes, scoring_ms_p50/p95/p99, norm_ms_p95, mem_peak_bytes, throttled_429_total, oversize_413_total. Alert if memory p99 rises above baseline.

Maria: Customer negotiation playbook: tell SearchX hosted GA supports up to 200 scored candidates; for 1k+ offer Dedicated pilot + pricing estimate and migration help. Provide sample client stitcher and rate-limiting guidance.

Zara: Launch checklist I propose: API spec + examples; SDKs updated with pager; perf benchmarks for top_k 10/25/100/200 hitting p95 targets; regression tests for score provenance and tie stability; docs/migration notes for pre_scores. GA rollout: start default GA for top_k<=50, staged opt-in to 200 via feature flag.

Ajay: I'll spin up the runtime PR for heap-based selection and attach perf numbers. Will include an opt-in approximate mode.

Deploy Bot: docs draft published internally: https://internals.redwood/re-rank/specs/draft-1840207890 

Maria: OK locking decisions for roadmap:
- API: candidates array + top_k + score_mode enum + page_token
- Default score_mode = none; normalized scores returned only when requested
- GA hosted caps: top_k default GA <= 50, scored candidates default <= 200; tenant may opt-in to 200 during rollout; >200 -> Dedicated
- Payload cap 4MB; per-candidate token cap default 512
- Errors: 413 for payload/format violations; 429 for tenancy throttles
- Deterministic tie-break by id and include sorted_by in response

Maria: I'll update the roadmap item and customer-facing template once docs and PRs are linked. Thanks all :rocket:
